outgoing.name: Banana
outgoing.excerpt: Its long jaws contained more than 60 banana-shaped teeth; larger tyrannosaurids possessed fewer teeth.

outgoing.name: Canada
outgoing.excerpt: The type species, A. sarcophagus, was restricted in range to the modern-day Canadian province of Alberta, after which the genus is named.

outgoing.name: Chicago
outgoing.excerpt: Fragmentary remains of smaller individuals were found alongside "Sue," the Tyrannosaurus rex mounted in the Field Museum of Natural History in Chicago.

outgoing.name: Fossil
outgoing.excerpt: Fossils of more than twenty individuals have been recovered, providing scientists with a more detailed knowledge of Albertosaurus anatomy than is available for other tyrannosaurids.

outgoing.name: Fossil record
outgoing.excerpt: Most age categories of Albertosaurus are represented in the fossil record.

outgoing.name: Toronto
outgoing.excerpt: The specimen originally named A. arctunguis was also excavated near the Red Deer River and is housed in the Royal Ontario Museum in Toronto, Canada.

outgoing.name: United States
outgoing.excerpt: Albertosaurus megagracilis (later renamed Dinotyrannus) was based on a small tyrannosaurid skeleton from the Hell Creek Formation of Montana in the United States.
